function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning: The user typed "time". They might want to know the current time? Or they might want to run the time command? In Windows, there's no 'time' command that prints the current time; you can use 'echo %time%' or 'powershell -Command Get-Date'. But the user just typed "time". We need to interpret. The user might want to get the current time. So we should respond with the current time. But we cannot call system commands because we don't have a function to get the time. We can just provide the time. But we don't have the actual time. We can approximate? We can respond with "The current time is ..." but we don't know the actual time. We could ask clarifying question. But maybe we can use the system command to get the time. We can call the function cmd_controller_execute with command 'powershell -Command Get-Date'. That will output the date/time. Let's do that.
